t: Capitalism is an economic system based on private ownership of the means of production and its use for profit, with capital accumulation, competitive markets, commodification and wage labour.

It emerged in its modern form from agrarian change in England and the mercantilism of the 16th to 18th centuries, and the Industrial Revolution of the 18th century made it the dominant mode of production.

Largely unregulated in the 19th century, it was regulated through Keynesianism after the Second World War and freed again under neoliberalism from the 1980s; after the Cold War it became a truly global system.
dyk: The word capitalism was coined by its critics: Louis Blanc used it in its modern sense in 1850 for “the appropriation of capital by some to the exclusion of others”, and in English it first appears, according to the Oxford English Dictionary, in Thackeray’s novel The Newcomes in 1854.
ev: England begins a large-scale and integrative mercantilism in the Elizabethan era
Adam Smith’s The Wealth of Nations describes competition as allocating resources to their most valued uses
Britain repeals the Corn Laws, abandoning the protectionism of mercantilism for free trade
Louis Blanc makes the first use of the word capitalism in its modern sense
Karl Marx analyses the capitalist mode of production in Das Kapital
The Sherman Antitrust Act becomes the first law passed by the United States Congress to limit monopolies
Friedrich Hayek argues in The Road to Serfdom that economic freedom is a requisite of political freedom
Margaret Thatcher takes office in Britain, and with Ronald Reagan’s presidency from 1981 monetarism gains prominence across the capitalist world

f.thinkers: Adam Smith, who made competition the foundation of a prosperous society; David Hume, critic of mercantilism; David Ricardo, advocate of free trade; Richard Cobden and John Bright of the Manchester School; John Maynard Keynes, of managed capitalism; Friedrich Hayek and Milton Friedman, who held economic freedom a requisite of political freedom; Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, its most influential critics
f.texts: Thomas Mun, England’s Treasure by Forraign Trade (written in the 1620s, published 1664); Adam Smith, The Wealth of Nations (1776); David Ricardo, Principles of Political Economy and Taxation (1817); Karl Marx, Das Kapital (1867); Max Weber, Economy and Society (1921); Friedrich Hayek, The Road to Serfdom (1944); Thomas Piketty, Capital in the Twenty-First Century (2013)
f.ideas: private ownership of the means of production; production for profit and the accumulation of capital; competitive markets and the price mechanism; wage labour; production of commodities for exchange; the freedom of owners to act in their self-interest; innovation and economic growth
f.today: the encompassing economic system worldwide, with the mixed economy its dominant form in the industrialised West; social market economies and Rhine capitalism in Western and Northern Europe and Japan; the Nordic model; state capitalism associated with the East Asian model and Norway; a fast-growing private sector in the People’s Republic of China
